title: Exploring Spatial and Temporal Patterns in the Size‐At‐Age of Pacific Halibut in the Gulf of Alaska
content:
ABSTRACT

Large changes in Pacific halibut (Hippoglossus stenolepis) size-at-age across decades have affected available fishery yield and management decisions. Characterizing mechanisms driving variability in size-at-age of adult Pacific halibut is challenging due to uncertainty associated with spatial and temporal partitioning of the phenomenon. We explored spatial and temporal changes in size-at-age structure of Pacific halibut in the Gulf of Alaska during 1998–2021, and the relationship between spatial patterns in size-at-age and diet using δ13C and δ15N analysis of muscle tissues collected in 2018. Pacific halibut size-at-age was spatially and temporally structured across the study area, with distinct regions of persistent anomalously high or low relative size-at-age. Further, trophic feeding level varied spatially and diet was related to size-at-age. Our results provide important context for investigations of specific mechanisms influencing Pacific halibut size-at-age and future research on Pacific halibut ecology. We recommend revisiting fundamental aspects of Pacific halibut biology, sampling methodology, and management practices from this spatiotemporal perspective.
